title: Paginated participants route has no linked coverage
reasoning: The owned change exposes a network endpoint for paginated fast participants, adjacent to the non-paginated participants route, but the included fast view tests only cover fast listing, feast-date lookup, and serializer day-number behavior. There is no first-class evidence that the new route resolves, enforces the intended auth/visibility rules, handles invalid fast IDs, or returns the expected paginated response contract. That leaves this route vulnerable to regressions in URL wiring or response shape without test failure.
recommendation: Add focused API tests for GET /hub/fasts/<fast_id>/participants/paginated/ covering a successful response, pagination fields, empty/unknown fast handling, and any intended permission or church scoping behavior.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests do not reference PaginatedFastParticipantsView, the fast-participants-paginated route name, or the participants/paginated URL path.
suggestedRegressionTest: In hub/tests/test_fast_views.py, create a fast with multiple profiles, call reverse('fast-participants-paginated', kwargs={'fast_id': fast.id}) or the concrete URL, and assert status 200 plus the paginated response shape and participant contents. Add negative cases for nonexistent fast_id and unauthorized access if the view requires authentication.
minimumFixScope: Add route-level/API tests for PaginatedFastParticipantsView without changing unrelated fast endpoint behavior.
